# Wildbloom Node

> Storing Blossom blobs on somebody else's server means somebody else can lose
> them, remove them or stop paying the bill. Wildbloom Node is a self-hosted
> Blossom storage server that turns a user's own machine into a standard
> Blossom node, reachable over a persistent Tor onion or an operator-managed
> HTTPS origin.

Wildbloom Node is for people who want to hold their own Nostr-addressed blobs
rather than trust a third-party Blossom host. It stores blobs on disk by
SHA-256, accepts only tightly scoped Nostr authorisation (BUD-11), and lets
another authorised node copy a blob across with BUD-04 mirroring. It is not a
torrent client or a WebRTC transport: every replica stores a complete blob and
serves it over ordinary Blossom HTTP.

## Getting Started

Wildbloom Node is not published to a package registry; build the headless
daemon from source.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/forgesworn/wildbloom-node.git
cd wildbloom-node
cargo build --release
./target/release/wildbloomd --allow-pubkey <64-lower-case-hex-public-key>
```

This binds the listener to loopback by default and starts a managed Tor
process unless `--no-tor` is given. Once ready, the log prints the stable
`.onion` Blossom URL to give to a Blossom-capable client.

Default mode needs the Tor Expert Bundle `tor` executable on `PATH` (or
`--tor-bin <PATH>`). If it is missing, `wildbloomd` exits during start-up with
an I/O `NotFound` error (on Unix, `Error: State(Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, ... })`)
that does not name tor. For a local test without Tor, run
`./target/release/wildbloomd --no-tor --allow-pubkey <hex>`.

To upload and read back a blob by hand, see "Test a node by hand" in
[README.md](README.md#test-a-node-by-hand).

## Key Concepts

- Content-addressed storage: blobs are indexed by the SHA-256 of the bytes
  actually received, never by a client-supplied filename or digest.
- BUD-11 authorisation: every write needs a short-lived, signature-checked
  Nostr kind `24242` event scoped to the exact operation, hash and server
  identity.
- Transport is separate from storage: Tor and direct HTTPS both carry bytes
  for the same underlying Blossom server; neither is required for storage
  itself.
- Retention tiers: an owner has full read/write; friends get expiring
  per-key byte ceilings via `--friend-grant`; `--open-shelter` admits
  unknown signed guest mirrors on spare capacity only, evicted first.
- Replica coordination: an optional headless coordinator can enrol blobs
  from an operator-supplied inventory and repair them across explicitly
  configured remote targets. See
  [docs/REPLICA-POLICY.md](docs/REPLICA-POLICY.md).

## API Surface

`wildbloomd` exposes standard Blossom HTTP endpoints:

- `GET` / `HEAD` on a blob's hash (BUD-01), with optional file extensions and
  single byte ranges. No authorisation is needed to read; an unknown hash is
  404.
- `PUT /upload` (BUD-02): streaming upload with `Content-Length` and
  `X-SHA-256`, authorised by a BUD-11 event in
  `Authorization: Nostr <base64-event>` (standard base64 per BUD-01; URL-safe
  and unpadded forms are also accepted). Any authorisation failure is 401.
- `PUT /mirror` (BUD-04): pulls a blob from another Blossom origin (onion via
  the private Tor SOCKS listener, or public HTTPS in direct mode).
- Authorised, self-only listing and claim-aware deletion (BUD-12), with
  bounded cursor pagination.

Key CLI flags (each also has a `WILDBLOOM_*` environment variable; see
`wildbloomd --help`):

- `--bind <IP:PORT>`: local listener, default `127.0.0.1:3742`.
- `--data-dir <PATH>`: data directory (`WILDBLOOM_DATA_DIR`), default per-user
  app data.
- `--quota-bytes <BYTES>`: total blob quota, default 10 GiB.
- `--max-blob-bytes <BYTES>`: largest single blob, default 1 GiB.
- `--allow-pubkey <HEX>`: owner public key, repeatable.
- `--friend-grant <PUBKEY:BYTE_LIMIT:EXPIRES_AT>`: friend key, byte ceiling and
  Unix expiry, repeatable.
- `--open-shelter`: admit unknown signed mirrors as guest data.
- `--device-grants`: accept owner-signed device grants on `/grants/v1`; needs
  `--allow-pubkey`.
- `--pairing-issuer`: issue one-use Foregather live grants to devices; needs
  `--device-grants` and `--pairing-relay-url`.
- `--pairing-relay-url <URL>`: Foregather resolver API base for
  `--pairing-issuer`.
- `--pairing-operator-token-file <PATH>`: private file holding the pairing
  operator token.
- `--turn-issuer`: issue short-lived TURN REST credentials to devices for
  direct send; needs `--device-grants` and `--turn-url`.
- `--turn-url <URL>`: `stun:`, `turn:` or `turns:` URL returned with each
  credential, 1 to 4, at least one TURN.
- `--turn-secret-file <PATH>`: private file holding the TURN server's
  `static-auth-secret` (or `WILDBLOOM_TURN_SECRET`).
- `--max-concurrent-writes <N>`: concurrent upload and mirror streams, default 4.
- `--repair-interval <SECONDS>`: integrity scan and repair interval, default
  3600; 0 disables repair.
- `--verify-storage`: verify every stored byte and exit.
- `--no-tor`: do not start managed Tor.
- `--tor-bin <PATH>`: Tor executable, default `tor`.
- `--public-url <URL>`: public origin for blob descriptors; needs `--no-tor`.
- `--direct-https-mirrors`: fetch public HTTPS mirrors directly; needs `--no-tor`.
- `--service-profile <PATH>`: opt-in public service listing.
- `--checkout-profile <PATH>`: opt-in paid checkout; needs `--no-tor`.

## Features

- Desktop app: native tray app with a Tor or direct choice and owner-directed
  storage pools. See [docs/DESKTOP-POOLS.md](docs/DESKTOP-POOLS.md).
- Storage pools: private signed receipts, part health checks and owner-side
  repair via `wildbloomd replicas pool-repair`. See
  [docs/POOL-STORAGE.md](docs/POOL-STORAGE.md).
- Service discovery: opt-in `GET /services/v1` snapshot and kind 31402
  publication via `--service-profile`. See
  [docs/SERVICE-DISCOVERY.md](docs/SERVICE-DISCOVERY.md).
- Paid checkout: Lightning and LNURLcash sales via `--checkout-profile`, off by
  default. See [docs/CHECKOUT.md](docs/CHECKOUT.md).
- Replica coordinator: `wildbloomd replicas run --policy <signed-policy.json>
  --state-dir <DIR> --owner <HEX>`, or `--policy-dir <DIR> --state-root <DIR>`
  for a directory of policies. See
  [docs/REPLICA-POLICY.md](docs/REPLICA-POLICY.md).
